title: Sensitive-data scanner findings, version 1.11
description: What one scan found in one account and region, or (1.4) in one site of the databases runner, or (1.6) in the Azure subscriptions of one site, or (1.7) in the Google Cloud projects of one site, or (1.8) in the SaaS tenants of one site: locations, classes, counts, confidence, offsets and coverage. Never a value. The same object is the detail of a 'Findings v1' EventBridge event, with 'part' and 'parts' added.

allOf.description: An AWS run names its account and region; a databases run (1.4), an Azure run (1.6), a Google Cloud run (1.7) and a SaaS run (1.8) name their site instead.

platform.description: Where the scanner ran (1.4). Absent: AWS, and the document names its account and region. 'database': the databases-anywhere container; 'azure' (1.6): the Azure scanner, whose findings and stores each name their subscription; 'gcp' (1.7): the Google Cloud scanner, whose findings and stores each name their project; 'saas' (1.8): the SaaS scanner, whose findings and stores each name their vendor and the hash of their tenant. Each names its site instead of an account and region.

site.description: The name the customer gave the place a non-AWS runner runs in (SCANNER_SITE): a data center, a cluster (1.4), an Azure management group (1.6), a Google Cloud organization or folder (1.7), where the SaaS scanner runs (1.8). Never a host or a connection string.

scanMode.description: The mode each platform ran in (1.8, #55): scanner (this scanner reads), vendor (the vendor's own detection, imported), or both.

vendorCoverage.description: Each importer's run (1.8, #55): whether it read the vendor's findings, how many, which kinds the vendor covers, and what it does not (limits).

atRestEncryption.description: The storage encryption the data sat under, from the store's own configuration (1.5): none, service_managed (a key the service holds: SSE-S3, an AWS owned or AWS managed key, a database's platform encryption), customer_managed_key (the customer's own key, named only by atRestKeyHash), or unknown.

atRestKeyHash.description: The SHA-256 of the customer managed key's id (the part after key/ in its ARN), lower-case hex (1.5). Never the key's id or ARN.

storeKind.description: A kind of store (1.3: one list for coverage, the run summary and listing errors; each kind after rds is new in 1.3; the databases runner's engines, from postgresql, are new in 1.4, and mysql covers MariaDB; stepfunctions, lambda, xray, codecommit, s3_directory, msk, mq, ecr, sagemaker, neptune_analytics, eventbridge_archive and glacier are new in 1.5; the Azure kinds, from azure_blob, are new in 1.6; the Google Cloud kinds, from gcs, are new in 1.7; the SaaS kinds, from m365_mail, are new in 1.8).

azureSubscription.description: An Azure subscription id (1.6), masked like a name.

resourceIdHash.description: The SHA-256 of the store's Azure resource ID, lower-cased, as lower-case hex (1.6). Never the ID itself, which names the resource group and the resource.

gcpProject.description: A Google Cloud project id (1.7), masked like a key.

resourceNameHash.description: The SHA-256 of the store's Google Cloud full resource name, exactly as Cloud Asset Inventory gives it (//storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>, //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/<project>/datasets/<dataset>/tables/<table>), as lower-case hex (1.7). Never the name itself.

saasVendor.description: The SaaS vendor whose tenant a finding or store is in (1.8).

saasHash.description: The SHA-256 of a SaaS identifier, as lower-case hex (1.8): tenantHash of the tenant's id (Microsoft 365: the Entra tenant id; Google Workspace: the customer id; Slack: the organization's or workspace's id; Atlassian: the site's cloud id; lower-case); ownerHash of a mailbox's or drive's owner (the user's principal name or address, lower-case: an address is PII, never written); itemHash of the vendor's id for the item. Hash yours the same way to match.

archivePath.description: In an archive (1.9, #65): the entry's path inside it, with '!/' between nested archives (outer.zip!/inner/x.csv), masked like a key. A .tar.gz or a .gz is one level.

archiveEntry.description: With archivePathMasked (1.9): the entry's position in its archive, one number per level (3/0), so two entries whose paths mask alike stay two findings. Nothing derived from the path is written.

contentKind.description: What an object is (1.9, #65), by its bytes or as its name claims.

maskedName.description: A name from the account (bucket, key, log group or stream, DynamoDB key value or attribute path). Any run that could be a card number or an SSN is masked with '#'.

bucket.description: The bucket name, masked like a key (1.2: '#' may appear).

column.description: For a table object (Parquet, ORC, Avro, or a catalog table's CSV or JSON): the column the values are in (1.2).

catalog.description: For an object read as part of a Glue Data Catalog table: its database and table (1.2).

table.description: The table name, masked like a key (1.2: '#' may appear).

keyHash.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the item's key under a salt kept in the scanner's state: stable across runs, never the key.

key.description: The item's key attributes, each value masked like an S3 object key.

attributePath.description: The attribute the values are in, with [] for every list element (stepResults[].observedDtmf). The offsets' pointers name the exact element.

planted.description: The path is configured as planted test input (a test script's steps), not a leak.

oneOf.description: One column of one table of an RDS or Aurora database (1.2): schema.table.column.

cluster.description: The DB cluster or DB instance identifier.

snapshotTime.description: When the exported snapshot was taken. Not part of the finding id.

oneOf.description: One field of a store that is not S3, logs, DynamoDB or RDS (1.3): a warehouse column, a search index's document field, a stream's or queue's records, a parameter's or secret's value. 'service' names the product.

store.description: The cluster, workgroup, domain, stream, queue, parameter or secret.

table.description: schema.table for a warehouse, or the index, keyspace table or shard.

field.description: The column, the document's or record's field, or 'value'.

snapshotTime.description: When the copy read was taken, for a snapshot. Not part of the finding id.

resourceGroup.description: The Azure resource group (1.6), masked like a key.

oneOf.description: One blob of an Azure Blob Storage or ADLS Gen2 container (1.6) and, for a table file, one column of it.

account.description: The storage account, masked like a key.

blob.description: The blob's name (an ADLS Gen2 path), masked like a key.

versionId.description: The blob version read, or 'null' when versioning is off.

column.description: For a table file (Parquet, ORC, Avro): the column the values are in.

resourceGroup.description: The Azure resource group (1.6), masked like a key.

oneOf.description: One file of an Azure Files share (1.7) and, for a table file, one column of it.

account.description: The storage account, masked like a key.

path.description: The file's path in the share, masked like a key.

column.description: For a table file (Parquet, ORC, Avro): the column the values are in.

resourceGroup.description: The Azure resource group, masked like a key.

oneOf.description: One object of a Google Cloud Storage bucket (1.7) and, for a table file, one column of it.

bucket.description: The bucket, masked like a key.

object.description: The object's name, masked like a key.

column.description: For a table file (Parquet, ORC, Avro): the column the values are in.

oneOf.description: One item of a SaaS tenant (1.8): a message, a file, a page or an issue, or a part of it (an attachment, a comment). Names are masked like keys; a person is named only by the hash of their address.

service.description: The vendor's product: exchange, onedrive, sharepoint, teams_channel, teams_chat (Microsoft 365); gmail, drive, shared_drive (Google Workspace); channel, dm (Slack); jira, confluence (Atlassian).

ownerHash.description: The mailbox's, drive's or chat member's owner, hashed (saasHash).

container.description: The site, team or channel set the item is in, masked like a key.

channel.description: The channel or document library within the container, masked like a key.

itemId.description: The vendor's id for the item (a Graph message or drive item id), masked like a key.

part.description: Which part of the item the values are in: message (a subject and body), attachment, file, reply, issue (a Jira issue's summary, description and comments), page (a Confluence page's title, body and comments).

name.description: The file's or attachment's name, masked like a key.

column.description: For a table file (Parquet, ORC or Avro): the column the values are in, masked like a key.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the string the offsets are in, for a JSON item.

link.description: A deep link into the account's own AWS console, (1.6) the resource's page in the Azure portal, (1.7) in the Google Cloud console, or (1.8) the item in its SaaS vendor's own web app, built from ids only (Outlook on the web by message id, a SharePoint document by its unique id, a Teams channel, a Google Drive file by its id, a Slack channel, a Jira issue by its key, a Confluence page by its id); null when a name it would carry had to be masked.

source.description: Who found it (1.8, #55): this scanner, or a vendor's own detection an importer read (vendor:macie, vendor:google_sdp, vendor:purview, vendor:google_workspace_dlp, vendor:slack_dlp). A vendor's finding has no offsets (format vendor, via vendor).

vendorType.description: The vendor's own detector type (1.8), its name only, masked: CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER, US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER. A type that maps to no spec class makes the class 'other'.

vendorFindingId.description: The vendor's id for its finding or alert (1.8), masked like a key.

linked.description: In both mode (1.8): the ids of findings of another source at the same location and class. Linked, never merged.

disguised.description: The object (or archive entry, or an archive holding it) is named as one kind and is another (1.9, #65): a Word document named .jpg. It was read by what its bytes are.

declaredType.description: With disguised (1.9): the kind the name's extension claims ('unknown' for an extension the scanner does not know). A kind, never the name.

detectedType.description: With disguised (1.9): the kind the bytes are.

rescanReason.description: (1.10, #67) The object did not change at its source and was read again because a component it was last read with changed and could change this result: its adapter, a reader it was read with, a new reader for a kind it held unread, the sniffer (for an object whose kind was undetermined or disputed), the standalone spec (text-bearing objects), the conversation spec (transcripts), or it had no row in the object index (read before the index knew it). Absent on a read for a change at the source.

duplicateOf.description: (1.10, #67) This object was not read: its bytes are those of another object of the same store, or (1.11) of another store of the same account, subscription or project (the same content fingerprint), read with the same components. This finding is that object's finding, as this object's own; duplicateOf is the other's finding id.

rescanClasses.description: (1.10) With rescanReason spec_standalone: the classes whose own rules changed, or that are new, when only those changed.

pciNote.description: Guidance for the customer's QSA, never a verdict (1.5): 3.3.1 for any cvv finding, whatever the encryption; 3.5.1.2 for a card finding under storage-level encryption (service_managed or customer_managed_key).

kmsDenied.description: Items not read because the scanner may not use their KMS key (1.2).

disguised.description: Objects and archive entries whose name claimed another kind than their bytes are (1.9, #65), counted whether or not anything was found in them. They were read by content.

indexed.description: (1.10, #67) Objects the source's object index holds after the run. Present when the source keeps an index.

rescanned.description: (1.10) Objects read again this run though unchanged at the source, by rescanReason.

duplicates.description: (1.10, #67) Objects not read because their bytes are an object this source already read, with components still current (the same content fingerprint): their findings are copies naming the original's (duplicateOf).

notAllowed.description: (1.10) Objects listed and not read because the store's own rules do not allow them, by reason: key_filter (the bucket's keyInclude / keyExclude in DISCOVER_SAMPLING). Counted, never read, never a finding.

rescanBacklog.description: (1.10) Rescans still owed: objects whose recorded components are stale, and objects with no row met and not read. Later runs read them within their capped share.

duplicatesAcross.description: (1.11, #67) Of duplicates, the objects whose bytes are an object of another store of the same account, subscription or project (found by the account's shared fingerprint table); their findings' duplicateOf names that store's finding.

relisted.description: (1.11, #67) How this kind of store is listed changed (its listing:<kind> component): this run listed it again from the start and read only what changed at the source or needed a rescan.

discovery.description: The run summary (1.2): every store discovered or named, including the ones not read and why. Present when discovery is on. In a multi-part event, 'stores' is split across the parts like 'findings'.

exportType.description: (1.10, #67) DynamoDB read by export: 'incremental' when this run's export holds only the items written since the last one (a full export is the default and is not named).

listedBy.description: (1.10, #67) An S3 bucket whose objects were found from its own S3 Inventory report instead of a listing.

recommendation.description: (1.10, #67) s3_inventory: an S3 bucket large enough that a daily S3 Inventory configuration would spare it a listing each pass. (1.11) s3_inventory_daily: a bucket read from a weekly inventory, whose changes can wait a week to be seen; blob_inventory: an Azure container large enough that a Blob Inventory policy would spare it a listing; storage_insights: a Cloud Storage bucket large enough that a Storage Insights inventory report would. The scanner never creates or changes one (a write), and reads only S3's.

deployment.description: Redshift: a provisioned cluster or a Serverless workgroup; OpenSearch: a managed domain or a Serverless collection (1.3).

database.description: The database a store is connected to by default (1.3).

resource.description: EBS: a volume (read through its latest snapshot) or the latest snapshot of a volume that no longer exists (1.3); SageMaker: a feature group or a notebook instance (1.5).

olderSnapshots.description: EBS: earlier snapshots of the same volume, counted and not read (1.3).

recoveryPoints.description: AWS Backup: the vault's recovery points by resource type (1.3).

destinations.description: Firehose: where the delivery stream delivers (1.3). Its S3 locations are read; Redshift and OpenSearch by their own kinds.

deadLetterQueue.description: SQS: another queue's redrive policy points at this one (1.3).

snapshots.description: ElastiCache and MemoryDB: the cache's snapshots, counted (1.3).

resourceGroup.description: Azure (1.6): the store's resource group, masked like a key.

tableType.description: BigQuery (1.7): the table's type (TABLE, VIEW, MATERIALIZED_VIEW, EXTERNAL, SNAPSHOT); only TABLE and SNAPSHOT are read.

protectedColumns.description: BigQuery (1.7): columns under a policy tag (column-level security), left out of the read.

hierarchicalNamespace.description: Azure Storage (1.6): the account has the hierarchical namespace on (ADLS Gen2).

api.description: Azure Cosmos DB (1.6): the account's API. Only sql (NoSQL) has an Entra data-plane read; the others are no_read_path, except a MongoDB vCore cluster.

networkRestricted.description: Azure (1.6): the store admits only selected networks or private endpoints; when the job is not among them, the store is the network gap.

writeGrants.description: The databases runner (1.4): the write privileges the database user holds, by name, when the store is refused (db_user_can_write). Never a value.

items.description: SSM Parameter Store and Secrets Manager: the parameters or secrets listed (1.3).

itemTypes.description: SSM: parameters by type (String, StringList, SecureString); Secrets Manager: secrets managed by another service or not (1.3).

excluded.description: Parameters or secrets not read, by reason: the deny or allow rules, unreadable tags, or SecureString with SSM_DECRYPT off (1.3).

fileSystemType.description: FSx: LUSTRE, WINDOWS, ONTAP or OPENZFS (1.3).

eventCount.description: An EventBridge archive: the events it holds (1.5).

retentionDays.description: An EventBridge archive: how long it keeps events; 0 is indefinitely (1.5).

archives.description: An S3 Glacier vault: the archives in it, as of its last inventory (1.5).

workflowType.description: Step Functions (1.5): a Standard state machine (its history is read) or an Express one (no history in the service; reported).

state.description: The store's own state, when it is why the store was not read (1.3).

backlogByKind.description: (1.11, #94) The stores still behind after this run, by kind: read in part (backlog) or not reached (deferred, reason budget). Empty when every pass is complete.
